tool_input.description: Extract task code into scratch dir and run tests

result:
I wrote the plan and its two task files. They validate, are set to `active`, and are committed as `9eab994` (`plan(WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001): activate`). Since we were on `main`, I created a new branch, **`plan/WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001`**, for the commit. I didn't execute the plan.

**Files** (in `specs/work/`):
- `WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001-mid-cycle-activation.md`
- `WRK-TASK-BILL-PRORATA-001-001-half-up-rounding.md`: sets up the project (`package.json`, Node's built-in test runner) and adds exact rounding to 2 decimals, half-up, in `src/rounding.js`.
- `WRK-TASK-BILL-PRORATA-001-002-pro-rata-amount.md`: adds `proRataAmount(monthlyFee, 'YYYY-MM-DD')` in `src/prorata.js`. It uses the calendar month as the billing period and bills the activation day, so day 15 of April is 16/30 and the last day of a month is one day.

**Checks:**
- Validation passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- I ran the plan's own code in a scratch directory outside the repo: all 16 tests pass.
- I swapped in the rounding code seen in `src/billing.js` (`Math.round(amount * 100) / 100`). The new tests catch it.

**Red-team review:** this ran because the domain spec has no `verified` entry and this is money logic. It found 6 problems, and I changed the plan for 5 of them:
- **Rounding:** my first approach pushed values just below .5 up. Rounding now uses exact integer arithmetic, so 1.005 → 1.01 and 1000.004999999999 → 1000.
- **Weak test:** one test couldn't tell the correct rounding from the old `Math.round` version. I added a case that can.
- **Very large fees** returned `Infinity`; they are now capped and rejected with an error.
- **Years 0–99** were handled wrongly by `Date.UTC`. Month lengths now come from a plain leap-year rule.
- **Negative amounts** are rejected. This is my choice, not something the domain spec says; I've recorded it in the plan so it gets settled when the work is closed out.

**Decisions for you:**
- **The real billing code isn't in this repo.** The rounding observation came from `billing-service`. This plan builds `proRataAmount` as a standalone module here, so mid-cycle activations will still be billed a full month in `billing-service` until it calls the new function. Wiring it in would need its own WRK-SPEC.
- **Activating a frozen spec normally needs recorded pins.** `WRK-SPEC-BILL-PRORATA-001` has no `activation_pins`. Validation doesn't require them here because the repo has no `kdd-repo.yaml`.

To execute later, run kdd-superpowers:subagent-driven-development on the branch. Its working files will go in `.kdd/sdd/WRK-PLAN-BILL-PRORATA-001/`.
